title: Adaptive probe backoff to reduce cold-start induced false scale-ups
creator: Priya Nambiar
description: During a recent capacity event we observed repeated, short-lived scale-ups triggered by health probe latency spikes during cold-starts. These false positives led to transient over-provisioning, degraded packing efficiency, and increased cost. This ticket proposes an adaptive probe-backoff mechanism that smooths noisy probe signals and biases scaling decisions away from single-sample spikes originating at pod startup.
impact: Transient over-provisioning across GPU pools for ~2 hours during peak traffic; ~15% increase in token cost for affected customers on dedicated pools; no customer-facing request errors but higher tail latency for downstream warmup calls.
timeline: 2026-02-25 08:12 UTC - Spike in probe latency observed on region-us-west-2 serving pool A

steps_taken: Added temporary smoothing to probe metric collector to weight recent samples less heavily at pod startup
Enabled a small warm pool for the affected serving topology to absorb cold-start probe noise
Rolled a conservative HPA patch to require 2 consecutive percentile breaches before scaling up
Opened distributed tracing on probe path to distinguish network vs. startup latency
root_cause: Two factors: (1) probe measurements at pod startup are dominated by model initialization and library lazy-loads causing p95/p99 to spike; (2) the autoscaler used a fixed percentile window that gave equal weight to startup samples, allowing single-pod cold-start spikes to drive cluster-level decisions.
analysis: Cold-start cost: new pods experienced 300-700ms additional latency while JITing kernels and initializing KV cache, which inflated percentile-based metrics
Metric aggregation: the percentile window was 60s with uniform sample weighting — this made short startup bursts visible at cluster scale when aggregated across many pods starting in a narrow window
Decision path: KEDA scalers used the aggregated probe percentile to generate scaling events without startup bias, and HPA immediately accepted the target change leading to quick, transient scale-ups
Observed pattern: warm-pool absence + rolling restarts (due to batch deployment) amplified simultaneous cold starts
action_items: Implement adaptive probe backoff: maintain a per-pod startup score that decays over 5 minutes and down-weights early probe samples in cluster aggregation
Introduce startup-aware percentile: when computing p95/p99 for HPA, exclude samples from pods flagged as 'initializing' or apply a configurable multiplier
Add two-step confirmation for scale-ups: require either sustained breach over 90s OR two independent metric windows (e.g., probe + CPU) to agree
Create synthetic warmup (light inference) job to pre-initialize model kernels during pod boot when warm-pool is not available
Add observability: dashboard tile that correlates pod age histogram with probe percentile spikes and cost impact
Test all changes in a canary dedicated pool and run load replay with staggered restarts before rolling to production
